summary: Custer County ground-mounted L-4 cab built 1934, evacuated in a 1988 fire, badly damaged in a 2010 windstorm, and now listed as gone.

facts.design: Ground-mounted L-4 cab, hip roof, 14 by 14 feet, with a catwalk
facts.status_note: Severely damaged in a 2010 windstorm and parts salvaged in 2011. A regional list marks it gone. No source describes what, if anything, remains.

staffing.status: Two named staff members, 1984 to 1989, per Idaho Fire Lookouts

access.note: Hike-in only, in the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness. The Register describes no road access.

visit.trail_note: The Register describes a steep ten-mile trail from the Indian Creek Ranger Station, on foot or horseback. Idaho Fire Lookouts tags it Hike-In. The cab is gone.

events.note: Ground-mounted L-4 cab with a hip roof, 14 by 14 feet
A fire spotter worked at the lookout in July 1957, per a newspaper item quoted by the Idaho lookouts site
A June 1958 item describes a planned summer posting at the tower. We found no later report confirming it.
Cole Nicole LeFavour listed as staff for 1984 to 1987
Christa Everett listed as staff for 1988 to 1989
A fire jumped the Salmon River toward the mountain in August 1988 and the lookout was evacuated
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on February 12, 2004. The register said it had been on emergency status for years and was in active service again.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 8,745 ft (2,665 m). Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 8813 ft. We do not state an elevation in the story and leave the brief's 2665.5 m unconfirmed.
The register names the Salmon Challis National Forest. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts name the Challis National Forest. The story does not name the forest.

notes_for_editor: Elevation and forest name differ between sources (see resolved_conflicts). The 1957, 1958 and 1988 items are newspaper excerpts transcribed on a fan site, not checked against the original papers. Staffing is only partly known. No source describes what remains at the site today, and the 2011 salvage does not say whether any structure stands. No photo with a usable URL was found.
